closing: Paralimni is the biggest town in the Famagusta district and the daily hub for Protaras, Pernera, Kapparis, Sotira, Frenaros, Liopetri and Deryneia. That mix shapes how you learn to drive here. In winter the streets are calm and great for first lessons, with quiet routes around Agia Anna, Agios Georgios and the back roads near the town hall. From May to October the picture changes fast. Tourist traffic from Protaras and Ayia Napa floods the main avenues, rental cars appear at every junction, and roundabouts like the one near the Paralimni stadium get busy from late morning onward. Learners who train through a full year get a real feel for both sides of Cyprus driving. Road conditions in Paralimni are generally good. The main routes are wide and well marked, but side streets in the old core are narrow with tight parking, and some village links toward Frenaros and Sotira have soft edges and no pavements. Expect tractors and farm pickups on the rural stretches near the red soil fields. The motorway link to Larnaca via the A3 is a key part of test prep, since many learners will use it for work or study. Instructors usually add a few sessions of higher speed driving, lane discipline and slip road merging before the test. The Paralimni driving test itself focuses on roundabouts, hill starts on the small inclines near Deryneia, reversing into a bay, and reading priority at unmarked junctions. Examiners watch closely for mirror use and smooth gear changes on manual cars. Local tips that come up again and again: practise the roundabout near the municipal market, learn the one way system in the centre, and get comfortable parking on a slope. Paralimni also has a strong cycling and scooter culture in summer, so hazard awareness around two wheelers is part of any good course. Choose a school that knows these streets, and your licence becomes much easier to earn in 2026.

faq.q: How old do I need to be to start driving lessons in Paralimni?
faq.a: You can apply for a learner permit at 17 and a half in Cyprus. You must hold the learner permit for at least six months before taking the practical test, so many Paralimni students start lessons soon after their 17th birthday.

faq.q: How many lessons will I need before the test?
faq.a: Most learners in Paralimni take between 20 and 30 hours of lessons. The exact number depends on prior experience, confidence on roundabouts, and whether you train on a manual or automatic car. Your instructor will give a clear view after the first few sessions.

faq.q: Where is the driving test held for Paralimni residents?
faq.a: Practical tests for the Famagusta district are run by the Road Transport Department, with test routes covering central Paralimni, Deryneia and nearby roads. Your school will take you over the likely routes during mock tests.

faq.q: Is it better to learn manual or automatic in Paralimni?
faq.a: Manual is still the standard choice in Cyprus and gives you a licence for both types. Automatic is good if you only plan to drive newer cars or find clutch control stressful. Plus Driving School can advise based on your goals.

faq.q: How much do driving lessons cost in Paralimni in 2026?
faq.a: Prices in 2026 generally range from 25 to 35 euro per lesson, with package deals for theory plus practical. Ask each school for a written quote that includes test fees, learner permit help and any pick up service from your home or work.
